key: Ask what the structure carries and where it runs: ovarian vessels mean infundibulopelvic, uterine vessels mean cardinal, the inguinal canal means round, and a peritoneal sheet means broad.
items: Carries the ovarian artery and vein
The ovarian vessels come from the aorta and enter the pelvis in this fold from the side wall to the ovary.
Clamped when an ovary is removed
Tying this pedicle controls the main ovarian inflow in an oophorectomy.
Ureter lies just medial to it at the brim
The ureter crosses the pelvic brim beside the ovarian vessels, so it is identified before clamping.
Twists with the ovary in torsion
Torsion twists the ovary on this vascular pedicle and cuts off its blood supply.
Carries the uterine artery and vein
The uterine vessels run medially along its upper border toward the cervix.
Ureter passes under the artery here
About 2 cm lateral to the cervix the ureter runs beneath the uterine artery on this ligament.
With the uterosacral ligaments it suspends the cervix and upper vagina. Its failure causes apical prolapse.
Also called the transverse cervical ligament, it is thickened fascia rather than a peritoneal fold.
It leaves the uterine horn and enters the deep inguinal ring, like the spermatic cord in men.
Its fibers blend into the labia majora, the female homolog of the scrotum.
The female gubernaculum attaches to the uterus, leaving the ovarian ligament above and this cord below.
Met during an indirect hernia repair in a woman
It occupies the female inguinal canal, so a surgeon repairing an indirect hernia meets it.
It is peritoneum draped over the uterus, tubes and ovaries, not a condensation of fascia.
Its named parts are the mesometrium beside the uterus, the mesosalpinx around the tube and the mesovarium.
As a thin sheet it carries structures but does not hold the uterus up against prolapse.
